canonical_definition: Hallucination Resistance refers to the capacity of AI systems, particularly vision-language and multimodal models, to avoid generating content unsupported by evidence, fabricating facts, or describing nonexistent visual elements. This construct encompasses robustness against various hallucination types (including category, attribute, and relation hallucinations) during generation and understanding tasks, with emphasis on maintaining accuracy and grounding in observed data. Some definitions further specify its role in enabling safer deployment through certified control over hallucinated content or its enhancement via discriminative training constraints, while others emphasize its measurement under adversarial questioning or via benchmarks like POPE.
